data.narrative:
Bedrock Ocean is a Series A-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Anthony DiMare and Charles Chiau. The company has raised $63M to date. The comparable universe for this sector remains sparse, with only two identifiable private peers (Seasats, Havoc AI) and no directly comparable public companies, reflecting the nascent state of frontier ocean tech.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the primary applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($63M) as a proxy for implied post-money value at entry, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $126M. This reflects the capital-intensity and risk profile characteristic of hardware-adjacent ocean technology ventures at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $107M (low) to $145M (high), centered on a median of $126M. Material uncertainties include the thinness of comparable transaction data in ocean tech, the absence of public market benchmarks for revenue or margin normalization, and the early-stage nature limiting visibility into unit economics or path to scale. The 2.0x multiplier assumption itself carries execution risk typical of frontier sectors. Given the limited comp set and single primary methodology, investors should treat this range as indicative rather than precise.
